title: Facebook Marketplace
summary: Browse and search nearby listings with separate spatial and keyword indexes and personalised recommendation ranking.
narrative:
Build Facebook Marketplace: sellers post a title, description, price, category, photos and location; buyers browse nearby listings, search by keyword with filters, and see a personalised recommended-for-you feed. Messaging and payments are out of scope. At ~1 B monthly users, expect ~10 M new listings/day, or ~115 writes/s. About 200 M daily browsers × ~20 queries generate ~4 B reads/day, or ~46 K/s.

Keep authoritative listing records in NoSQL keyed by listing id, with photos uploaded through the Web Server to Blob Storage and served via CDN. Five photos averaging ~300 KB per listing produce ~15 TB/day. A Geospatial Index uses geohash cells to retrieve listings within 40 km, checking neighboring cells and exact distance at boundaries as in Yelp / Nearby Friends (level-18). A separate Search Index handles keywords, categories and price filters; combine spatial and keyword candidates when both filters are present.

Route API traffic through a Load Balancer to redundant Web Servers. Publish listing-created and listing-updated events to a Message Queue; a Worker updates both indexes asynchronously, with versioned idempotent updates to avoid old events overwriting newer listings. Hydrate results from NoSQL and check current listing status before showing unavailable items. For recommendations, take candidates from the nearby set and recent searches, then rank with an ML Model Server using predicted click or purchase likelihood. Optional Cache stores hot listings and per-user recommendations; Monitoring tracks index lag and query failures.

functional: Create and update listings with title, description, price, category, photos and location
Store listing records by id in NoSQL and photo bytes in Blob Storage behind the CDN
Browse within 40 km via a geohash Geospatial Index; search keywords with category and price filters via Search Index
Publish listing change events and asynchronously update both indexes with a Worker
Rank nearby and recent-search candidates with an ML Model Server for personalised recommendations
nonFunctional: Handle ~115 new listings/s and ~46 K reads/s on average
Allow short indexing lag while checking authoritative listing status on result hydration
constraints: Clients must not access NoSQL or Search Index directly
Connect both Search Index and Geospatial Index to the Worker that applies listing events
Check adjacent geohash cells and exact distance; combine spatial and keyword filters when requested
Messaging and payments are out of scope
capacity: ~1 B monthly users; ~10 M new listings/day ≈ 115 writes/s
~200 M daily browsers × ~20 queries ≈ 4 B reads/day ≈ 46 K/s
specs.tradeoff: Separate spatial and keyword indexes fit different access patterns but require asynchronous updates and result reconciliation. ML ranking can personalise candidate order while cached hot results reduce read load; neither ranking nor indexing should replace authoritative listing-state checks.
specs.bonus: Connect Web Servers to Cache for hot listings and per-user recommendations, and add Monitoring for query failures and index lag.

resilienceRules.message: Run at least two Web Servers so Marketplace survives one instance failure.
Connect Search Index to a Worker that applies listing changes.
Connect Geospatial Index to a Worker that keeps location cells current.

hints: Split Client → CDN → Blob Storage for photo reads from Client → Load Balancer → Web Server for APIs. Connect the app to NoSQL for listings and Blob Storage for photo uploads.

Connect Web Server → Geospatial Index for nearby results and → Search Index for keywords and filters. As in Yelp (level-18), include adjacent cells then check exact distance. Connect Web Server → ML Model Server to rank nearby and recent-search candidates.

Run two Web Servers, each connected to NoSQL, Blob Storage, Geospatial Index, Search Index, ML Model Server and Message Queue. Wire Message Queue → Worker → Search Index and Geospatial Index. Add each Web Server → Cache and → Monitoring.
